slides.texte_overlay:
questions smart people ask
themselves every day

what did i learn today

they end each day by naming one thing they learned. a day where you can't answer this question is a sign to change something about tomorrow, even something small.

what am i assuming

before a big decision, they ask what they're taking for granted. most bad choices come from assumptions nobody checked, not from a lack of information.

what don't i know yet

they spend 5 minutes a day learning about something they know nothing about: art, science, history. asking what you don't know yet is how your world keeps getting bigger.
slides.texte_sophia:
what don't i know yet

i spend 5 minutes a day on something i know nothing about: art, science, history. i do it with the Sophia app, one lesson a day, and my world keeps getting bigger.

slides.texte_overlay:
who could teach me this

when they're stuck, they ask who already knows the answer. there's almost always someone who solved your problem before, and most people love being asked.

what would i tell a friend

when they're hard on themselves, they ask what they'd say to a friend in the same place. it's the fastest way to swap panic for a calm, useful answer.
